extracted.intended_audience: plant breeders, seed growers, and applicants seeking plant variety protection
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance about the Plant Variety Protection Act (PVPA) and the Plant Variety Protection Office which issues Certificates of Protection for qualifying new plant varieties; aimed at breeders seeking legal IP protection. Covers scope (types of reproduction covered) and the administering office/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of protection (types of plant propagation covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides legal intellectual property rights protection to breeders of new varieties of plants which are sexually reproduced (by seed) or tuber-propagated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for PVPA protection is limited to new plant varieties that are either sexually reproduced (by seed) or propagated by tubers; varieties propagated by other asexual means are not mentioned on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory framework: Plant Variety Protection Regulations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PVPA is implemented under specific regulations (the Plant Variety Protection Regulations) which govern how protection is granted and administered. (This page references the regulations but does not display their detailed criteria.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration: Plant Variety Protection Office issues Certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plant Variety Protection Office administers the Plant Variety Protection Act (PVPA), by issuing Certificates of Protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for protection are processed and Certificates of Protection are issued by the Plant Variety Protection Office; procedural steps, requirements, and examination criteria would be handled by that office (details not included on this page).
